name: skills-marketplace
description: Community skill catalog for opencode/Claude agents

skills.name: api-design
skills.description: Use when adding or changing HTTP endpoints, request/response contracts, validation, error handling, pagination, versioning, REST routes, GraphQL schemas, or OpenAPI documents

skills.name: best-practices
skills.description: Use as the default baseline when writing or changing production code that has no more specific skill attached — readable, correct, testable, maintainable code

skills.name: brainstorming
skills.description: Use when a task is open-ended — how should we, options for, design a — without a chosen direction, or when comparing approaches and trade-offs before committing

skills.name: code-review
skills.description: Use when reviewing a diff, pull request, or code change before it merges — check correctness, security, and maintainability

skills.name: database-migrations
skills.description: Use when adding or changing tables, columns, constraints, indexes, backfills, data transformations, or schema definitions — design safe, reversible, performant migrations

skills.name: docs-writing
skills.description: Use when adding or updating READMEs, API docs, inline docs, or operational runbooks, and when changed behavior or contracts must stay in sync with documentation

skills.name: frontend-ux
skills.description: Use when building or changing components, pages, routes, or styling, and for accessibility, responsiveness, or design-system conformance in any frontend framework

skills.name: performance
skills.description: Use when investigating slowness, latency, throughput, scaling, or missed SLOs, and when profiling, optimizing, or troubleshooting queries, caching, and hot paths

skills.name: refactoring
skills.description: Use when asked to improve, clean up, simplify, restructure, deduplicate, extract, or rename existing code without changing its observable behavior

skills.name: security-hardening
skills.description: Use when a change handles user input, authentication, authorization, secrets, SQL, HTML rendering, deserialization, or any data flow across a trust boundary — apply OWASP-informed secure coding and threat modeling

skills.name: test-first
skills.description: Use when a task adds or changes behavior you can observe and assert, or fixes a bug — write the failing test first and drive the change through red-green-refactor
